statement: In randomized trials of people receiving chemotherapy (28 trials, 1,772 participants, mostly of nabilone, THC, levonantradol or dronabinol; 23 at high and 5 at unclear risk of bias), cannabinoid medicines compared with placebo are associated with more people having complete control of nausea and vomiting: in a 2015 meta-analysis of the three placebo-controlled parallel-group trials that could be pooled (dronabinol or nabiximols; Whiting et al., 2015; AMSTAR 2 critically low), 47% on cannabinoids against 20% on placebo had a complete response (percentages given only in the abstract, their derivation not described; about 27 more in 100, editors' arithmetic), OR 3.82 (95% CI 1.55 to 9.42; 102 patients; I2 0%; low certainty by the review team). Twenty trials compared cannabinoids only with other anti-sickness medicines, most often prochlorperazine (13 of the 20, editors' count from the review's Table 1; 15 trials in all had a prochlorperazine arm). The review says, without pooled figures, that all the trials pointed towards more benefit with cannabinoids than with the other medicines or placebo, though not significantly in all; because these comparisons are not pooled, how cannabinoids compare with those medicines, or with the anti-sickness medicines in use today, is not shown here. A narrative review calls THC an effective treatment for nausea and vomiting with chemotherapy, citing one source, and says, without a cited source, that patients often find marijuana more effective (Volkow et al., 2014; second-hand). Certainty: low. Status: replicated.
plain: In three small trials (102 people having chemotherapy), about 47 in 100 people who took a cannabis medicine (dronabinol or a THC and CBD spray) had their sickness fully controlled, against 20 in 100 who took a dummy medicine (placebo). Most of the other trials compared cannabis medicines with other anti-sickness medicines; the review says these leaned towards the cannabis medicines too, but it did not combine them and not every result was clear. Most trials had weaknesses in how they were run or reported.
population: People receiving chemotherapy in randomized trials published up to April 2015
exposure: Cannabinoid medicines as given in the trials (in the pooled placebo comparison, dronabinol or nabiximols; across all trials mostly nabilone, THC, levonantradol and dronabinol); doses are study conditions
comparator: Placebo (pooled); other anti-sickness medicines, mostly prochlorperazine (not pooled)
outcome: Complete response (complete control of nausea and vomiting as each trial defined it)
magnitude: Whiting et al. 2015, cannabinoid (dronabinol or nabiximols) against placebo, parallel-group trials, random effects: complete response 47% vs 20% (given only in the abstract; about 27 more in 100, editors' arithmetic), OR 3.82 (95% CI 1.55 to 9.42; 3 trials, 102 patients; I2 0%; GRADE low by the review team). Comparisons with active anti-sickness medicines (20 trials; prochlorperazine in 13 of them, editors' count from Table 1) not pooled in the article; the review says all trials favoured cannabinoids, not significantly in all.

evidence.locator: Results › Nausea and Vomiting Due to Chemotherapy; Table 1 (comparator column, THC rows); Table 2 (nausea and vomiting row); Abstract › Results
evidence.extracted: Nausea and vomiting due to chemotherapy: 28 studies (37 reports; 1772 participants): 14 nabilone, 3 dronabinol, 1 nabiximols, 4 levonantradol, 6 THC; 8 placebo-controlled (3 with an active arm as well) and 20 against an active drug only; the most common active comparator was prochlorperazine (15 studies, counting 2 three-arm trials that also had placebo); risk of bias high in 23, unclear in 5. Complete response, cannabinoid (dronabinol or nabiximols) against placebo: OR 3.82 (95% CI 1.55 to 9.42), 3 trials, 102 patients, I2 0%, GRADE low; the abstract gives 47% against 20%, a figure not derived in the article (study card reporting issue). No pooled comparison with active drugs is reported.

evidence.extracted: Risk of bias across the 79 trials (Cochrane tool): 4 low, 55 high, 20 unclear; the main source was incomplete outcome data, with more than half of trials reporting substantial withdrawals not adequately handled; 57% reported appropriate blinding of participants and 24% of outcome assessors.

evidence.locator: Results › Nausea and Vomiting Due to Chemotherapy, 1st paragraph; Table 1 (comparator column, rows for levonantradol, nabilone, THC and dronabinol)
evidence.extracted: The review states, without pooled figures, that all studies suggested a greater benefit of cannabinoids than of both active comparators and placebo, not reaching statistical significance in all. Table 1 lists prochlorperazine as comparator for levonantradol (2 trials), nabilone (7), THC (3 against prochlorperazine alone and 2 against placebo and prochlorperazine) and dronabinol (1, against dronabinol plus prochlorperazine or prochlorperazine): 15 trials, as the text says. The 2 THC trials with a placebo arm are among the 8 placebo-controlled trials, so prochlorperazine was the comparator in 13 of the 20 trials with only an active comparator (editors' count). Ondansetron was a comparator in a single trial (dronabinol, ondansetron, the two combined, or placebo).

risk_of_bias.note: 23 of the 28 trials at high and 5 at unclear risk of bias (card sc_whiting_2015); psychoactive effects may unblind patients.

indirectness.note: Worded against placebo; how cannabinoids compare with the anti-sickness medicines used today is not shown by this pool.

imprecision.note: Three trials with 102 patients; the interval runs from 1.55 to 9.42.

publication_bias.note: Not investigated by the review; not downgraded separately.

grade.reasoning: Randomized trials start high; down one for risk of bias and one for imprecision: low, matching the review team's rating. Status replicated: three placebo-controlled trials pooled without heterogeneity (I2 0%). The comparisons with other anti-sickness medicines, which make up most of the trials, are not pooled in the article and are not rated here; the narrative review's view is second-hand and only qualifies.
